proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is the right (ius) to alienate, destroy, or dispose of a thing — one of the three classical sticks of dominium (usus, fructus, abusus). It is a legal power/entitlement that inheres in an owner (a material entity, a person) relative to a res, and is grounded externally in the legal system that recognises it. BFO Role (BFO_0000023) is correct: it is externally grounded (requires a legal order to confer it), inheres in a bearer (the dominus), and can be realised in acts of alienation or destruction. It is best modelled as a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight class, which already sits under BFO_0000023.

entities.label: ActOfDisposition
entities.rationale: Abusus is realised in acts of alienation, destruction, or encumbrance of the res. These are occurrents — processes in which the owner (bearer of Abusus) participates. Minting ActOfDisposition as a Process subclass provides the target for the BFO_0000054 (realized in) relation.

entities.label: Dominium
entities.rationale: Roman full ownership (dominium) is the bundle role that comprises usus, fructus, and abusus. Modelled as a Role subclass of LegalRight so that Abusus can be typed as a component right that is part of Dominium.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of LegalRight (itself a Role), inheriting BFO_0000023 typing.
Dominium is the bundle of property rights, itself a LegalRight/Role.
Abusus is a component right that is part of the bundle constituting Dominium — subclass relation captures the genus-species inclusion.
The role Abusus is realised in (instances of) ActOfDisposition — the owner exercises the right by performing an act of alienation or destruction.

open_questions: Should Abusus be modelled as an individual instance (the specific ius recognized by classical Roman law) rather than a class? If the discussion remains at the level of a general kind, class is appropriate; if this conversation is about a single historically fixed concept, an individual would be better.
Do you want usus (right of use) and fructus (right to fruits) minted as sibling classes under Dominium for completeness?
Should ActOfDisposition be further specialised into ActOfAlienation (transfer) and ActOfDestruction, or is the single class sufficient for current purposes?
Is Dominium intended to be the bearer of Abusus (i.e., Abusus inheres in the person qua Dominus), or should we also mint a Dominus role class to serve as the canonical bearer?

The BFO_0000050 (part of) relation is sometimes used for component rights within a bundle — should we assert working:Abusus BFO_0000050 working:Dominium at the instance level, or is the subClassOf relation sufficient for your purposes?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus — the Roman-law power to alienate, destroy, or encumber a res — is best typed in BFO as a Role (BFO_0000023). It is an externally grounded specifically dependent continuant: it inheres in a particular bearer (the dominus) and owes its existence entirely to the recognising legal order, not to any intrinsic property of the bearer. This makes it a Role rather than a Disposition. Because the working ontology already has LegalRight as a subclass of BFO_0000023, Abusus is most conservatively placed as a subclass of LegalRight, preserving the existing hierarchy. Dominium (full ownership) is minted as the bundle Role of which Abusus is a component, also under LegalRight. The right is realised in occurrents classed as ActOfDisposition (BFO_0000015 Process), connected via BFO_0000054 (realized in). Three entities are proposed as new classes; no new individuals are required unless the discussion pivots to a specific historical enactment.
